messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected for api-gateway in us-west1 (gateway-prod). Spike started ~1801234510. Paging on-call.

sarah (oncall): seeing it. looking at dashboard now — errors are mostly 502/504 timeout-ish from model-proxy upstream.

Raj Patel: joining — what services are returning the 5xx? gateway logs or proxy?

Chen Li: tailing gateway logs now, lots of `upstream reset` and `connect() failed` entries. sample:```
2026-03-14T14:02:11Z gateway[gw-12]: error: http2: client connection closed: connection reset by peer
2026-03-14T14:02:12Z gateway[gw-13]: warn: upstream model-proxy/pm-03 - 502 Bad Gateway
```

Miguel Alvarez: this started right after a burst of long-running inference at ~14:00. Could be connection churn in model-proxy or an open file/socket exhaustion. any mem OOMs?

Taylor (SRE): no OOMs on nodes. socket stats show an increase in TIME_WAIT and SYN_RECV on the proxy pool. possible kernel ephemeral port exhaustion; also seeing higher p95 latency to the model host.

Raj Patel: oncall -> elevating. Miguel, can you confirm if autoscaler for model-proxy triggered? If not, we can temporarily shift traffic.

Miguel Alvarez: autoscaler didn't kick — HPA shows current replicas 6, target 6. CPU not saturated but concurrency is high. suspect blocking inside service (thread pool exhaustion).

sarah (oncall): customers: a few enterprise customers reported degraded requests and timeouts via support. customer-support, can you estimate impact?

customer-support: we have 3 active tickets referencing error 502/504 in last 10m, two are critical (SLAs). They're mostly in us-west region. Forwarding customer IDs to oncall in DM.

Taylor (SRE): mitigation plan proposal: 1) circuit-break model-proxy to reduce retries 2) shift 30% traffic from us-west1 to eu-west1 for public endpoints 3) enable lightweight fallback model variant for sensitive customers 4) scale model-proxy horizontally and bump file descriptor limits.

Raj Patel: +1. Let's do controlled reroute first to relieve load. How fast can load balancer policy change?

Miguel Alvarez: we can do an incremental routing weight change via traffic-router: ```
# shift 30% from us-west1 to eu-west1 for route /v1/generate
traffic-router update --route /v1/generate --weights us-west1=70,eu-west1=30
``` Applying now in 30s. Expect 2-3s to propagate to edge.

incident-bot: ACTION: traffic-router change applied by miguel at 1801234625 — us-west1=70, eu-west1=30. Monitor for error rate drop.

Chen Li: after shift, 5xx rate in us-west backend dropped ~40% in 90s, overall user-facing errors down 25%. latency to eu-west increased median by 60ms for routed traffic. No new error modes observed there.

sarah (oncall): good. Next: scale model-proxy pool to 12 replicas, bump ulimit on deployments, and enable circuit breaker lowering retries. Who can push?

Taylor (SRE): I can handle k8s scaling and ulimit. Running:```kubectl scale deploy/model-proxy -n prod --replicas=12``` and patch to set `ulimit nofile: 65536` via initContainer.```

deploy-bot: Deploy started: scale/model-proxy -> replicas 12 by Taylor at 1801234700.

Raj Patel: I will reduce gateway retry policy and lower upstream concurrency:```yaml
gateway.retry: max_attempts: 1
gateway.upstream_concurrency: 32
``` Applying as hot config.

Miguel Alvarez: also enabling fallback smaller-model for tiered customers to reduce per-request resource.  command: `feature-flag enable fallback-small-model --scope region:us-west1`

incident-bot: NOTE: feature-flag change by miguel at 1801234752 - fallback-small-model enabled for us-west1 (gradual rollout).

Chen Li: logs now show fewer connection resets and model-proxy pod CPU is pegging higher but handling requests. 5xx rate trending down to baseline within 6 minutes of initial change.

customer-support: customers updated: two critical customers were routed to eu-west successfully, one still seeing occasional timeouts but working. Support is offering credit + immediate follow-up.

sarah (oncall): okay looks stabilized but we should keep traffic weight reduced and follow up with a postmortem. Raj, can you take incident lead for the postmortem and capture timeline + root cause hypothesis? I'm going to hand off on-call to you in 10m.

Raj Patel: taking lead. I've created incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incident/1801234567 (please add logs and timestamps). Key hypothesis: resource starvation inside model-proxy under long-running inferences causing socket churn and upstream resets.

Taylor (SRE): I'm going to leave the scale + ulimit changes in place and will revert traffic weights back to normal only after metrics stable for 30m and after a model-proxy configuration patch that hardens thread pool is deployed.

Miguel Alvarez: I'll open an action item to add better connection pool metrics and increase HPA target to account for long-running tails.

sarah (oncall): handing off: I'm signing out of on-call. Summary for you Raj: elevated 5xx in us-west1 due to model-proxy socket churn; mitigated via 30% cross-region reroute, scale up to 12 replicas, ulimit bump, reduced retries, enabled fallback model. Customer impact: 3 tickets, 2 critical; errors down and partial routing helped restore.

Raj Patel: acknowledged — I'll own the follow-up. Tagging @pg for postmortem review. Creating incident label P1-limited-regional-degradation.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. Priority: P1-limited-regional-degradation. Incident lead: Raj Patel.

Chen Li: quick note - captured `strace` of a broken proxy process showing `EMFILE` around time of spike. attaching to incident doc.

Taylor (SRE): I'll add runbook step to increase ephemeral port range and add netstat checks to oncall checklist.

customer-support: continuing outreach to affected customers; will keep updates in ticket thread.

Raj Patel: thanks everyone. We'll keep monitoring for 60m. If rates re-escalate, we'll escalate to L4 and consider fallback to dedicated capacity for affected tenants.

sarah (oncall): thanks team, leaving thread. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident actions logged: reroute, scale, ulimit-patch, retry-policy-change, fallback-model-rollout.
